title: Add an rbAmp module
noApi: This hub's firmware can't add modules from the app. Update the hub firmware.
loadFailed: Couldn't read the hub's module list: {why}
full: The hub already has {max} modules — its maximum.
whyFree: Every rbAmp module leaves the factory at address 0x50, and two modules can't share an address. So the module that sits at 0x50 now moves to a free address first, and the new one is then connected at 0x50.
freeWhat: Module {module} {model} moves to {to}. The module stores the new address itself; its points keep their names, history and settings.
freeAbsent: Module {module} is at 0x50 but isn't answering. Check its connection, then check again — its address can only change while it answers. If your modules are set to other addresses, press «Find one at another address» instead.
noFreeAddr: No free address is left in 0x51–0x5F.
moved: Module {module} now answers at {addr}. Address 0x50 is free for the new module.
step1Unplug: To remove a module, unplug its whole cable, not only the power: a module left on the bus without power stops the readings of every module.
step2: Connect ONE new module to the hub's I2C connector next to the others (SDA, SCL, GND, VCC). Only one at a time: it arrives at 0x50.
step3: Switch the hub on, open this window again and press Scan.
pullup: Keep each module's cable up to 15 cm. With up to three modules, leave the modules' pull-ups as they are — no cutting, no extra resistors.
pullup4: With four or more modules, cut the pull-ups on all but one module (or fit one external pair) — see the wiring guide.
busStuck: A bus line is held low — a module may be without power, set to another mode (e.g. Modbus) or wired wrong. Check the module connections, then scan again.
noneFound: No new module answered. Check that it is connected and powered, and that it is the only new one, then scan again.
others: Also on the bus, not rbAmp modules: {list}
addedNext: Its channels are under «Free sensors» on this page — bind them as points.
noneElsewhere: No new module answers at another address. A new module from the box is at 0x50 — move the module above first.
adoptWhy: Module {module} at 0x50 is an empty slot: nothing is measured on it. A new module from the box answers at 0x50 and takes this slot as module {module} — no address change, no scan.
adoptStep2: Connect ONE new module to the hub's I2C connector (SDA, SCL, GND, VCC), then switch the hub on.
adoptStep3: Give it 10–20 seconds after switching on, open this window again and press «Check again»: the module shows as present, and its channels appear in Points as free sensors to bind.
